conventions.convention: A = Z[q,q⁻¹]; A₀ and A∞ are the rational local rings regular at zero and infinity. Integral chart intersections are Z[q]- and Z[q⁻¹]-modules, whereas their simultaneous intersection is a Z-module.

Integral balancedness means that M ∩ L₀ ∩ L∞ maps isomorphically onto (M ∩ L₀)/(M ∩ qL₀), not directly onto the entire rational crystal space. The definition applies componentwise on finite root or label spaces.

Transport Lusztig's parameter by v = q⁻¹ and K_hᴸ ↦ K_−h, fixing root generators and divided powers. The transported source coproduct is the opposite library coproduct. On degree ν, B_L = C_ν B_K with C_ν = ∏ᵢ(1−qᵢ²)⁻νᵢ.

The normalized Drinfeld pairing is D(x,y) = d_ν⁻¹ B_K(ιx,y), where ι(Eᵢ)=Fᵢ and d_ν=∏ᵢ(qᵢ−qᵢ⁻¹)νᵢ. Its generator value is 1/(qᵢ−qᵢ⁻¹), and its Borel adjunctions use Δ on the negative side and Δᵒᵖ on the positive side.
The quasi-R completion is positive first and negative second. Θ₀=1 and Δ(u)Θ=Θ barΔ(u). Completed families are evaluated only after establishing vectorwise finite action.
The integral string projector uses ordinary powers of eᵢ′. I_(i,n)ᴬ is a left string-image ideal; its module image is initially only an A-submodule. Module saturation is proved after globalization.
Negative-half reversal is a linear anti-involution fixing Fᵢ. This batch proves signed crystal-residue preservation; it does not assert an unsigned star-crystal theorem.

The upper lattice is the restricted graded form-dual of the lower integral lattice. Upper vectors are inverse-Gram duals, fixed by the form-adjoint upper bar. Upper Kashiwara operators are weighted adjoints; their zero-chart reductions agree with the lower crystal operators.

Finite integral quasi-R action and triangularity do not imply finite supported corrected lifts. Arbitrary finite-type based pairs receive the action theorem; globalization additionally requires the specified supported construction class or finite raw-basis correction closure.

The globalization arguments retain AC inherited through the grand-loop, negative-half form and generic PBW-rank suppliers. The finite chart, string and dual-coordinate calculations introduce no additional choice.

load_bearing.statement: For every symmetrizable datum in the explicitly chosen label-weight category, the negative-half and dominant highest-module integral crystal triples are balanced componentwise. Their lower lifts are bar invariant and actual A-bases, adapted to all divided string-image ideals; projection sends each half lift to zero or the corresponding module lift. For eᵢb=0, G∞(fᵢⁿb)−Fᵢ⁽ⁿ⁾G∞(b) belongs to I_(i,n+1)ᴬ.

At height r, assuming integral balancedness and global lifts at all smaller heights for the half and all dominant highest modules, including lower-height based projection and adapted half membership, every I_(i,n)ᴬ and J_(i,n)ᴬ with n≥1 is integrally balanced in the specified degree, with the stated integral string residues and free Laurent extensions.

For a finite-dimensional Q(q)-space with a spanning A-submodule and full free rational chart lattices, integral balancedness gives the stated Z[q], Z[q⁻¹], A and rational-chart extensions of the simultaneous intersection. A simultaneous lift module generating M over A and injecting into both rational residues gives balancedness; the stated relative criterion applies modulo an already balanced submodule.

For dominant λ, π_λ:U_A⁻→V_A(λ) is a based quotient: a lower global vector maps to zero exactly when its crystal image vanishes, and otherwise to the corresponding module lower global vector. Its integral kernel is ΣᵢΣ_(s>λ(hᵢ)) U_A⁻Fᵢ⁽ˢ⁾.

The D-coevaluation family in the diagonal root-height completion is the unique normalized solution of Δ(u)Θ=Θ barΔ(u), with Θ₀=1 and the two displayed generator recursions. On the i-th root axis, Θ_(nαᵢ)=(qᵢ−qᵢ⁻¹)ⁿ[n]_(qᵢ²)! Eᵢ⁽ⁿ⁾⊗Fᵢ⁽ⁿ⁾. Evaluation requires the completion's explicit finiteness hypotheses.

In the same positive-first/negative-second completion, Θ⁻¹=barΘ. The displayed coproduct and barred-coproduct factorizations hold with their specified orders and middle toral factors, and ((Δ⊗id)Θ)Θ₁₂=((id⊗Δ)Θ)Θ₂₃ coefficientwise and on vectors with finite iterated actions.

Integral action holds for highest-first pairs, lowest-second pairs, arbitrary based finite-Cartan-type pairs, and the specified C_high/C_low based constructions under their action conditions. Supported tensor globalization has the additional stated support or finite correction-closure requirements. Finite-type universal integral coefficients are proved; unrestricted affine coefficients and arbitrary based-pair affine action can fail.

For U⁻ or V(λ), the upper family is an actual A-basis of the restricted graded integral form-dual, with weightwise perfect pairing against the lower lattice. Its genuine dual-chart triple is balanced, its upper bar fixes its vectors, and its weighted adjoint operators reduce to the same zero-chart crystal.

For the specified periodic based sl₂ chain, every finite cut J≥1 has a unique normalized fixed seed lift. Its coefficient at each retained odd endpoint j=2k+1 is independent of the cut and congruent to (−1)ᵏ(2k+1)!(q³−q) modulo q⁴+1. Raw-coordinate projection sends larger-cut lifts exactly to smaller-cut lifts; every cut has a nonzero correction with constituent index at least J−1.

alerts.finding: Step 5.1 says: 'The finite quasi-R intertwiner satisfies Θ barΔ(u)=Δ(bar u) Θ'. The cited batch-8 theorem instead gives Θ barΔ(u)=Δ(u) Θ. The printed identity fails for u=K_h: barΔ(K_h)=K_h⊗K_h, whereas Δ(bar K_h)=K_−h⊗K_−h. The subsequent Eᵢ/Fᵢ calculation uses bar-fixed generators and is unaffected; correct the generic displayed identity or explicitly restrict it to those generators.
